titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§158–164: The Pursuit of Buiruq Qan, Jamuqa's Slander, and the Pact at the Black Forest
part: §§158–164 — The Pursuit of Buiruq Qan, Jamuqa's Slander, and the Pact at the Black Forest
about: Seven sections. §158: Chinggis Qahan and Wang Qan ride against the Naiman Buiruq Qan, chase him over the Altai and along the Urungu, and destroy him at Lake Kishil-Bashi. §159: on the way back they meet Kögse'ü-Sabraq's Naiman army drawn up at Baidaraq-Belchir; they agree to fight at dawn, but Wang Qan leaves his fires burning and slips away in the night. §160: Jamuqa, moving off with Wang Qan, slanders Temüjin in a figure of two birds, and Ubchigtai Kürin Ba'atur rebukes him. §161: Chinggis finds the camp empty and follows. §162: the Naiman pursuers plunder Senggum's household, and the two Merkid sons rejoin their father. §163: Wang Qan begs for Chinggis's four heroes, who rescue Senggum and the people. §164: Wang Qan, old and short of sons, makes Temüjin a son, and the two swear a pact of campaigning, hunting, and distrust of slander. The Ming glosses carry most of the weight, and several clauses are marked in the notes as first readings or not understood.

sentences.t: Teġün-ü qoina Čiṅgis Qaγan, Waṅ-Qān qojar Naiman-u Köčügüd-ün Buiruγ- Qān-dur morilažu
sentences.l: That-of after, Čiṅgis Qaγan, Waṅ-Qān, the-two, Naiman's Köčügüd's Buiruγ Qān-to, mounting,
sentences.i: After that Chinggis Qahan and Wang Qan, the two of them, rode against Buiruq Qan of the Naiman Köchügüd,
sentences.n: Teġün-ü qoina, 'that-of after', is a stock opening: 'after that'. Buiruγ- and Qān-dur are one name split by the line ending (Shiratori prints the hyphen). The two genitives, Naiman-u Köčügüd-ün, I read as describing Buiruγ Qān, 'the Naiman's Köchügüd's Buiruq Qan'; the Ming glosses Köčügüd '(clan-)and-name', and how it attaches to the name I cannot tell, so I keep it as printed. morilažu is morin 'horse' (mori before -la-) + -la- + -žu, Ming 上馬着 'mounting', so 'mounting against', riding out against him. It opens a converb chain (mounting; when being; arriving) that runs on into the next unit, where the subject changes to Buiruγ Qān; the cut falls after morilažu.

Wang Qan, a ruler's name (Ming 人名 'a person's name') [人名]
the two, a pair (of persons) [兩箇]
Köchügüd, a clan-and-name (Ming 姓名; analysis uncertain) [(姓名的)]
Buiruγ, a man's name (the printed hyphen runs on to the next word) [人名]

sentences.t: Uluγ-Taγ-un Soqoγ-Usun-a büküi-dür kürčü Buiruγ Qān baildun jadažu Altai daban ködöl- be.
sentences.l: Uluγ-Taγ's Soqoγ-Usun-at being-when, arriving, Buiruγ Qān, battle-facing, being-unable, Altai crossing, moving-was.
sentences.i: When they reached him at the Soqoq Usun of Uluq-Taq, Buiruq Qan could not face battle; he crossed the Altai and moved off.
sentences.n: büküi-dür is 'at being' (bü- + -küi + -dür, Ming 有時 'when it is'); the subject of the 'being' is not stated, and I take it that Buiruγ Qān was at the river when they came up. That is a first reading. baildun comes from a stem baildu- that I infer from Ming 對陣 'face in battle array'; jadažu from Ming 不能着 'unable'. ködöl- and be are one word, 'moved', split across the line (stem, then past -be). daban is Ming 過 'cross over', a converb.

morph.gloss: Uluγ-Taγ, a place name [地名 的]
Soqoγ Usun, a river name (usun is 'water') [水名行]
to face in battle order, join battle (stem inferred from the Ming 對陣) [對陣]
to cross over a pass or ridge [過]
to move, set out (the stem; its past ending stands on the next word) [動]

sentences.t: Soqoγ-Usun-ača Buiruγ-Qān-(n)i nekežü Altai daba- γ̇ulun Qumšiṅgir-un Uruṅγu huruγ̇u hüldežü jabuqui-dur
sentences.l: Soqoγ-Usun-from, Buiruγ-Qān-ACC pursuing, Altai crossing-over, Qumšiṅgir's Uruṅγu along chasing, going-when,
sentences.i: From Soqoq Usun they pursued Buiruq Qan, crossed the Altai, and as they went chasing him along the Urungu of Qumshingir,
sentences.n: Another stretch of the chain, cut here; it is a time clause ('when going', jabuqui-dur) and its main verb comes in the next unit. daba- and γ̇ulun are one word split by the line; the ending is glossed only 了 'finished'. I read it as perhaps causative -γ̇ul- + converb -n (as in the published qariγ̇ulun, 'making return'), which would be 'having got across'; that is a guess. huruγ̇u, Ming 順 'following', I take as 'along' a river.

to cross over (the stem; its ending stands on the next word) [過]
causative (a guess, as in qariγ̇ulun); the Ming glosses only 了 'finished' (analysis uncertain) [了]

sentences.t: Jedi-Tubluγ neretü nojan in-ü qaraγ̇ul jabužu bidan-u qaraγ̇ul-a hüldegdežü aγ̇ula öġede dutaγ̇aqu bolun olaṅ-ni-jan tasuraγdažu tende bariγdaluγ̇a.
sentences.l: Jedi-Tubluγ named lord his, scout going, our scout-by being-chased, mountain upon fleeing-about becoming, own-girth-ACC being-cut, there was-seized.
sentences.i: A lord of his named Jedi-Tubluq, going on scout, was chased by our scouts; as he was about to flee up a mountain his girth was severed, and he was seized there.
sentences.n: in-ü 'his' follows its noun nojan, as the possessive does in the published parts, 'a lord of his'; it points back to Buiruγ Qān, so Jedi-Tubluγ is on the enemy's side, going as a scout (qaraγ̇ul jabu-); the Ming for qaraγ̇ul-a is 出哨的行 'to the scouts out on patrol', and the dative after a passive (hüldegdežü) marks who does the chasing. dutaγ̇aqu: I do not know the stem; the Ming 要走 'about to run' is all I have, with -qu 'about to'. olaṅ is Ming 肚帶 'belly-band'; tasuraγdažu is 'being cut through', passive of a stem I take from Ming 被斷着. So his girth gave way as he fled: the text implies it without saying why.

morph.gloss: his (third-person genitive, front-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]
n inserted before a case ending
on top of, upon (postposition; Ming 上) [上]
to flee, run (stem uncertain; inferred from the Ming 要走 'about to run') [要走]
converb: -ing (the Ming 呵 makes it 'if, when')

sentences.t: Uruṅγu huruγ̇u hüldeġed Kišil-Baši naγ̇ur-a güjičežü Buiruγ Qān-(n)i tende muqudγaba.
sentences.l: Uruṅγu along chasing, Kišil-Baši lake-at catching-up, Buiruγ Qān-ACC there wiped-out.
sentences.i: Chasing on along the Urungu, they caught up with Buiruq Qan at the lake Kishil-Bashi and there destroyed him.
sentences.n: The subject is not named; it is the allies of the opening unit. muqudγa- is the stem met in §154 (Ming 窮絕 'ruined and cut off'), and naγ̇ur is Ming 海子 'lake', the Chinese word for an inland lake.

morph.gloss: along, following (a river) (postposition; Ming 順 'following') [順]
to catch up with, overtake (Ming 趕上) [趕上着]
to wipe out, destroy (stem inferred from the Ming 窮絕 'ruined and cut off') [窮絕了]

sentences.t: Tendēče Čiṅgis Qaγan Waṅ-Qān qojar qarižu aisuqui-dur Naiman-u qadqulduγči Kögseġü-Sabraγ, Baidaraγ-Belčir-e čerig žasažu qadqulduqu bolun ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: There-from, Čiṅgis Qaγan, Waṅ-Qān, the-two, returning, coming-when, Naiman's fighter, Kögseġü-Sabraγ, Baidaraγ-Belčir-at, army arraying, fight-about becoming, was.
sentences.i: From there Chinggis Qahan and Wang Qan, the two of them, turned back; and as they were on the way, the Naiman fighter Kögse'ü-Sabraq was drawing up his army at Baidaraq-Belchir, about to give battle.
sentences.n: Tendēče is tende 'there' + -ēče with a long vowel. aisuqui-dur is Ming 來時 'when coming': aisu- 'come' as in the published parts, with the participle -qui and -dur. Shiratori has no stop between the 'when coming' clause and the next, so they stand in one unit. qadqulduγči is qadqul- 'fight' + reciprocal -du- + agent -γči, Ming 厮殺的 'those who fight'. I take Naiman-u qadqulduγči as an epithet of the man named next, which Shiratori sets off with a comma ('the Naiman fighter, Kögse'ü-Sabraq'); the Ming does not settle whether it is a title or a plural noun. ažuγ̇u is a- 'to be' + -žuγ̇u, Ming 有來 'was'.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Wang Qan, a ruler's name (Ming 人名 'a person's name') [人名]
the two, a pair (of persons) [兩箇]
to come (stem uncertain; Ming 來 'come') [來時 時]
to put in order, array (Ming 整治) [整治着]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan, Waṅ-Qān qojar qadqulduja keġen čerig žasažu kürčü žilda boldažu manaγaru qadqulduja keġen žerge-ġer qonoba.
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, Waṅ-Qān, the-two, fight-let-us, saying, army arraying, arriving, evening having-become, tomorrow-at-dawn fight-let-us saying, in-line bivouacked.
sentences.i: "Let us fight," said Chinggis Qahan and Wang Qan, the two of them, and having put their army in order and come up, when evening fell they said, "Let us fight at dawn tomorrow," and bivouacked in line.
sentences.n: -ja is the first-person-plural 'let us', Ming 咱; keġen closes each quoted thought, and the sentence runs on to qonoba (no stop in Shiratori before it). The Ming's 兩箇 'the two' is qojar, kept in l as 'the-two'. boldažu is bol- + -da- + -žu, Ming 被做着, 'having become'; žilda is Ming 晩 'late, evening'. manaγaru carries an ending -u I cannot explain (Ming 明早, 'tomorrow early'). žerge-ġer: žerge 'line' + instrumental, Ming 列着 'in rows'.

to put in order, array (Ming 整治) [整治着]

sentences.t: Tende Waṅ-Qān baidal-dur(i)-jan γal-nuγ̇ud tüleġülžü süni böġed Qara-Seġül öġede ködölžüġüi.
sentences.l: There Waṅ-Qān, own-camp-at, fires burning-caused, night then, Qara-Seġül up-against moved-was.
sentences.i: There Wang Qan had fires kept burning at his own camp, and then, in the night, moved off up the Qara Segül.
sentences.n: tüleġülžü is tüle- 'burn' + causative -ġül-, Ming 敎燒着 'having caused to burn'. The fires left behind look like a ruse, but this unit does not say so. böġed (Ming 便 'then') is the glossary's böġed, perhaps bü- + -ġed, 'then, thereupon'; uncertain. öġede, 'on top of' in §158, is glossed 逆着 'against' here; I take it as 'against the current, up' the river Qara Seġül (Ming 水名). baidal-dur(i)-jan: the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel, -jan is 'own'.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, a ruler's name (Ming 人名 'a person's name') [人名]
then, thereupon (Ming 便; perhaps bü- 'to be' + converb -ġed, as in the glossary; uncertain) [便]
Qara Segül, a river name [水名]
up, against the current, upstream (Ming 逆着 'against'; the word that means 'on top of' elsewhere) [逆着]

sentences.t: Tende Žamuqa Waṅ-Qān-luγ̇a qamtu ködölülčežü jaburun Waṅ-Qān-(n)a Žamuqa ügülerün:
sentences.l: There, Žamuqa, Waṅ-Qān-with together moving-together, going-when, Waṅ-Qān-to Žamuqa speaking:
sentences.i: There Jamuqa was moving off together with Wang Qan, and as they went Jamuqa said to Wang Qan:
sentences.n: -luγ̇a (Ming 一同) 'with'; ködölülčežü is ködöl- 'move' + an extension I read as 'together' (Ming 共動着), but the exact suffixes are uncertain. jaburun is jabu- + -run, 'when going'. The colon opens a speech that runs to keġežüġüi, seven units on.

morph.gloss: extension: 'together' (cf. -ulča- in abulčaja; analysis uncertain; Ming 共動)

sentences.t: "Temüžin anda min-u uridāča Naiman-dur elčitü büleġe.
sentences.l: "Temüžin, sworn-brother mine, from-before Naiman-to envoys-having was.
sentences.i: "Temüjin, my sworn brother, has had envoys among the Naiman from long ago.
sentences.n: anda, Ming 契交, is the sworn brother, a bond made by oath. elčitü is elči 'envoy' + -tü 'having'; uridāča is urida 'before' + a long ablative, Ming 自在前 'since earlier'. büleġe is the narrative past 'was' (as in §154). The charge is made by Jamuqa; here it is only a statement.

morph.gloss: sworn brother (Ming 契交 'pledged friend') [契交]

sentences.t: Edöġe ese irebe.
sentences.l: Now not came.
sentences.i: Now he has not come.
sentences.n: ese is the negative of a past action (Ming 不曾). The subject is not stated; the Ming 來了 'came' fits Temüjin, but I leave it as a first reading.

morph.gloss: not (negates a past action; Ming 不曾) [不曾]

sentences.t: Qān! Qān!
sentences.l: Qan! Qan!
sentences.i: Qan! Qan!
sentences.n: A doubled vocative, an address to Wang Qan (the Ming has 皇帝 for each); Shiratori's exclamation marks.

sentences.t: Aqu qairuγana bi bijü že.
sentences.l: Staying white-feathered-bird, I, am (statement).
sentences.i: I am the white-feathered bird that stays.
sentences.n: The figure of the two birds begins. Aqu is a- 'to stay' + -qu, Ming 存的 'the remaining'. qairuγana, Ming 白翎雀兒 'white-feathered little bird' (雀兒 is a small bird, sparrow-sized), names a bird whose species I do not know; I say 'bird' and name none. bi is 'I' and bijü 'is', so 'I am'. že is Ming 也者, a closing particle. Jamuqa casts himself as the bird that stays and, next, Temüjin as the one that goes; the images themselves are not explained in the text.

morph.gloss: a small bird, species unknown (Ming 白翎雀兒 'white-feathered little bird') [白翎雀兒]
emphatic particle at the end of a statement (Ming 也者) [也者︀]

sentences.t: Ažiraqu bilduγ̇ur anda min-u bijü.
sentences.l: Parting heaven-announcing-bird, sworn-brother mine, is.
sentences.i: My sworn brother is the heaven-announcing bird that goes away.
sentences.n: Ming 吿天雀兒 for bilduγ̇ur, 'announce-heaven little bird': another small bird, again not named. ažiraqu is ažira- 'to scatter, part' (Ming 散的) + -qu; I infer the stem from the gloss (the glossary has ažiraba, 'turned back', Ming 囘去, which may be the same verb).

morph.gloss: to scatter, part (stem inferred from Ming 散; cf. ažiraba 'turned back', Ming 囘去) [散的]
a small bird, species unknown (Ming 吿天雀兒 'heaven-announcing little bird') [吿天雀兒]
sworn brother (Ming 契交 'pledged friend') [契交]

sentences.t: Naiman-dur odčuγ̇ui že.
sentences.l: Naiman-to went (statement).
sentences.i: He has gone to the Naiman.
sentences.n: odčuγ̇ui is od- 'go' + the past -čuγ̇ui (Ming 去了). že closes the statement as before.

morph.gloss: emphatic particle at the end of a statement (Ming 也者) [也者︀]

sentences.t: Oroqu bolun qočo- rba" keġežüġüi.
sentences.l: Taking-refuge-about becoming, fell-behind," saying-did.
sentences.i: "Meaning to go over to them, he has dropped behind," he said.
sentences.n: Oroqu is oro- 'enter' + -qu (Ming 要投 'about to throw himself on / take refuge'). qočo- and rba are one word split by the line break: qočor- 'to fall behind' (Ming 落後) + -ba. I read the whole speech as a veiled accusation that Temüjin is deserting to the Naiman; the glosses themselves say no more than that he has envoys there, has not come, and has gone behind. The quotation mark closes at rba.

morph.gloss: to enter, take refuge (Ming 要投) [要投的]
to fall behind (the first part of the stem qočor-; the r stands on the next word) [落後]
the last letter of the stem qočor- [了]

sentences.t: Žamuqa-jin tere üge-dür Ubčiγtai Kürin- Baγ̇atur ügülerün:
sentences.l: Žamuqa's that word-in, Ubčiγtai Kürin Baγ̇atur speaking:
sentences.i: At these words of Jamuqa, Ubchigtai Kürin Ba'atur said:
sentences.n: üge-dür is 'in the word' (Ming 言語裏). Ubčiγtai is glossed 姓(名), a surname-like name; Kürin is a name, and Baγ̇atur (Ming 勇士) is the title 'hero, brave warrior'. The hyphen after Kürin- is Shiratori's line-ending hyphen.

morph.gloss: Jamuqa, a man's name [人名 的]
Ubchigtai, a clan name (Ming 姓名) [姓(名)]
Kürin, a man's name (the printed hyphen runs on to the next word) [人名]

sentences.t: "Žusuridču jakin tein šilγ̇un aqa deġü-jüġen ülkinžekün ügülejü" keġebe.
sentences.l: "Fawning, why so gentleman brothers-own slander speaking-is," said.
sentences.i: "Why does a gentleman fawn like this and speak slander against his own brothers?" he said.
sentences.n: A first reading and a doubtful one. Žusuridču: I infer the stem from Ming 諂侫着 'fawning'. šilγ̇un is Ming 君子 'gentleman, man of standing'; I take it as the subject and a sarcastic address to Jamuqa, but it could equally stand apart. aqa deġü, 'elder (and) younger brother', is the pair 'brothers', which the Ming glosses separately (兄, 弟); -jüġen is 'own'. ülkinžekün (Ming 讒譖 'slander') I do not analyse.

morph.gloss: to fawn, flatter (stem inferred from Ming 諂侫) [諂侫着]
gentleman, a person of standing (Ming 君子; sense uncertain) [君子]
slander, backbiting (Ming 讒譖; not analysed further) [讒譖]
converb or ending: 'is speaking' (Ming 說有)

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan süni mün tende qonožu qadqulduja keġen manaγar erte üdür geiġülün Waṅ-Qān-(n)u baidal-dur üžeġesü ügei boldažu
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan, night that-very there having-passed, fight-let-us, saying, tomorrow early day dawning, Waṅ-Qān's camp-at looking-when, not-being having-become,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan spent that same night there, saying, "Let us fight," and next morning, when day broke and he looked at Wang Qan's camp, it was gone,
sentences.n: qonožu is qono- 'pass the night' + -žu (Ming 宿). mün is Ming 只 'just', here 'that very'. manaγar erte üdür is three words, 'tomorrow, early, day' (Ming 明早 晨 日). geiġülün: Ming 明 'bright'; 'when it grew light'. ügei boldažu is 'having become not-being' (bol- + passive -da- + -žu, Ming 被做着); I read it as 'was empty' and say 'gone'. The chain goes on through the quoted words of the next unit; its main verb is baγ̇uba, in the next unit, and I cut the chain there for readability.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
that very, the same (Ming 只 'just') [只]
optative, first person plural: let us (Ming 咱)
to grow light, dawn (Ming 明; cf. geiġešü in the glossary) [明]
converb: 'when it dawned' (the ending, perhaps causative -ġül- + -n, is uncertain)

sentences.t: "Edeči bidan-i tülešilen ažuγ̇u" kēġed tendēče Čiṅgis Qaγan ködölžü Eder-Altai-jin belčir(i)-jer Ketülžü tere ködölügse-ġer ködölžü Saγ̇ari-Keġer baγ̇uba.
sentences.l: "These, us-ACC, cooked-meal-making were," saying, there-from Čiṅgis Qaγan moving, Eder-Altai's valley-mouth-by crossing, that moved-which-by moving, Saγ̇ari-Keġer came-down.
sentences.i: "These have been making a cooked meal of us," he said; from there Chinggis Qahan moved off and crossed the Eder Altai by its valley mouth, and, going by the way already travelled, halted at Sa'ari-Ke'er.
sentences.n: Not understood. The Ming for tülešilen is 做燒飯, which is 'make a meal of cooked rice'; I first took 燒 as 'burnt', but 燒飯 is simply cooked food, and I give it as it stands, without 'burnt'. It may refer to the fires left burning in §159, but that is a guess and I do not know the idiom. Edeči is ede 'these' + -či, an ending the Ming does not explain (it glosses 這的每 'these'). bidan-i is 'us' with the accusative; ažuγ̇u 'were'. kēġed is keġe- 'say' + -ġed, run together with a long vowel. belčir(i)-jer: Ming 谷口 'mouth of a valley'; the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel and -jer I take as the instrumental -ġer after i, 'by way of'. ketülžü is ketül- 'to cross, ford' (Ming 渡着). Eder-Altai is Ming 地名 'a place name'. The last clause is hard: ködölügse-ġer is ködöl- 'move' + a past participle + instrumental, Ming 動了的依着 'in accordance with what moved'; tere is 'that'. Whose earlier movement is meant (Wang Qan's, or Chinggis's own) the glosses do not say; I read it as 'by the route already taken'; 'route' is my word, the glosses have only 'in accordance with what moved'. baγ̇uba is baγ̇u- 'to come down' (Ming 下, used of halting and camping).

morph.gloss: ending of unclear sense (Ming 這的每 gives only 'these')
n inserted before a case ending
a cooked meal, food cooked (Ming 做燒飯 'make a meal of cooked rice'; analysis and idiom uncertain) [做燒飯︀]
to say (the stem; keġe- + -ġed run together and written kē-) [說了]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Eder-Altai, a place name [地名 的]
instrumental: by way of (the -ġer ending after i)
past participle (-gse(n) after a linking vowel, as in the glossary's ködölügseġer): 'that which moved' (Ming 動了的)
instrumental: by, according to (Ming 依着)
to come down, halt, make camp (Ming 下) [下了]

sentences.t: Tendēče Čiṅgis Qaγan, Qasar qojar Naiman-u tubuγ̇ud-i uqažu haran-a ese toγ̇olai.
sentences.l: There-from Čiṅgis Qaγan, Qasar, the-two, Naiman's outline-ACC understanding, people-to not reckoned.
sentences.i: From there Chinggis Qahan and Qasar, the two of them, grasped the Naiman's general outline, but did not reckon it to the people.
sentences.n: Doubtful throughout ('outline' is for Ming 大槩 'in general'; no plan or design is in the glosses). tubuγ̇ud is Ming 大槩 'in general, roughly' and I do not know the stem; uqažu is uqa- 'understand' (Ming 省着 'grasping'). haran-a is Ming 人行 'to the people', and ese toγ̇olai is Ming 不曾筭來 'did not reckon'. I follow the glosses word for word and cannot tell whether it means they said nothing to the army, or did not count the people in, or something else.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
the two, a pair (of persons) [兩箇]
the general outline, the gist (Ming 大槩; stem uncertain) [大槩行]
accusative or dative: object marker (Ming 行)
not (negates a past action; Ming 不曾) [不曾]
to count, reckon (Ming 筭; the stem toγ̇a- of the glossary, here written toγ̇o-) [筭來]
past tense ending (Ming 來; cf. -laγ̇ai; form uncertain)

sentences.t: Kögseġü-Sabraγ Waṅ-Qān-(n)u qoināča nekežü Seṅgüm-ün eme köġü irge orγa selte daγ̇uližu abču
sentences.l: Kögseġü-Sabraγ, Waṅ-Qān's from-behind pursuing, Seṅgüm's wife, son, people, household with plundering, taking,
sentences.i: Kögse'ü-Sabraq pursued Wang Qan from behind, and plundered and took Senggum's wife and son, with his people and household,
sentences.n: qoināča is qoina 'behind' + the ablative (Ming 後行). Waṅ-Qān-(n)u is a genitive, so 'from behind Wang Qan'. selte is 'together with' (Ming 連 'including'), so the list is taken as a whole. The subject is Kögse'ü-Sabraq, the Naiman fighter of §159; here he plunders the rear of Wang Qan's column, which is why Wang Qan sends to Chinggis in the next §.

morph.gloss: to pursue, harry (Ming 追襲 'chase and attack') [襲着]
household, tent-folk (Ming 人烟 'smoke of people') [人烟]

sentences.t: Waṅ-Qān-(n)u Telegetü amasar-a bükün žarimud irge aduγ̇un ideġe daγ̇uližu abuγ̇ad qarižuγ̇ui.
sentences.l: Waṅ-Qān's Telegetü pass-at being some people, livestock, food plundering, taking, returned.
sentences.i: He plundered and took part of Wang Qan's people who were at the Telegetü pass, with their livestock and food, and turned back.
sentences.n: bükün is 'the ones who were' (Ming 有的); žarimud is Ming 一半每 'a half / some (plural)', and whether 'half' or 'some' I leave open. amasar-a: Ming 口子 'mouth', so a pass or defile. ideġe 'food' (Ming 喫食 'something to eat').

morph.gloss: pass, defile (Ming 口子 'mouth') [口子 行]
some, a part (Ming 一半) [一半每]
livestock, herd animals (Ming 頭口) [頭口]
food, something to eat (Ming 喫食) [喫食]

sentences.t: Tere soγ̇or-tur Merkid-ün Toγtoγ̇a-jin Qutu, Čilaγ̇un qojar köġüd tende bürün irge-ben abuγ̇ad qaγačažu ečige-dür(i)-jen neilen Seleṅge huruγ̇u ködölžüġüi.
sentences.l: That skirmish-in, Merkid's Toγtoγ̇a's Qutu, Čilaγ̇un, the-two sons, there being, people-own taking, leaving, father-own joining, Seleṅge along moved-was.
sentences.i: In that clash, Qutu and Chila'un, the two sons of Toqto'a of the Merkid, who were there, took their own people, left, joined their father, and moved off along the Selenge.
sentences.n: soγ̇or-tur: the Ming 引鬭 'lead-fight' (a lured fight?) is all I have for soγ̇or, so I say 'clash' without confidence. Qutu and Čilaγ̇un are the two sons (Ming 子名, 子每); bürün is bü- 'be' + -rün, Ming 有呵 'being'. irge-ben is 'their own people' with -ben. qaγačažu is qaγača- 'part from' (Ming 離着) with no stated object; I take it as leaving the battle. ečige-dür(i)-jen: dative 'to', with the bracketed linking vowel, + 'own'; neilen is Ming 相合 'joining'. huruγ̇u 'along' is as in §158.

morph.gloss: a lured fight, skirmish (Ming 引鬭 'lead-fight'; sense uncertain) [引鬭 裏]
Toqto'a, a man's name [人名 的]
Chila'un, a man's name (Ming 子名 'son's name') [子名]
the two, a pair (of persons) [兩箇]
converb of time: being (Ming 有呵)
to part from, leave (Ming 離) [離着]
to join, unite (Ming 相合) [相合]
along, following (a river) (postposition; Ming 順 'following') [順]

sentences.t: Kögsegü-Sebraγ-a daγ̇uliγdažu Waṅ-Qān Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur elči iležüġüi.
sentences.l: Kögsegü-Sebraγ-by having-been-plundered, Waṅ-Qān, Čiṅgis Qaγan-to envoy sent.
sentences.i: Plundered by Kögse'ü-Sabraq, Wang Qan sent an envoy to Chinggis Qahan.
sentences.n: Shiratori spells the man's name differently here (Kögsegü-Sebraγ) from §162 (Kögseġü-Sabraγ); the Ming 人名 reads it the same, so I take one man. The -a after a passive daγ̇uliγdažu is the agent, 'by' (Ming 行). iležüġüi is ile- 'send' + past (Ming 差去了).

morph.gloss: dative: by (the agent of a passive; Ming 行)
Wang Qan, a ruler's name (Ming 人名 'a person's name') [人名]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: Elči ilerün: "Naiman-a irge orγo-ban eme köġü-ben daγ̇uliγdaba bi.
sentences.l: Envoy sending-when: "Naiman-by, people, household-own, wife, son-own, were-plundered, I.
sentences.i: As he sent the envoy he said: "The Naiman have plundered me of my people and my household, my wife and my son.
sentences.n: The message is Wang Qan's, though Shiratori's colon follows the envoy. ilerün is ile- + -rün, 'when sending'. The reflexive endings -ban and -ben mean 'own'. The sentence ends in bi, Ming 我 'I', as the next one will too: a repeated 'I' closing each statement.

morph.gloss: dative: by (the agent of a passive; Ming 行)

sentences.t: Köġün-eče-ġen dörben külüġüd-i čin-u γujužu ilebe. bi.
sentences.l: Son-from-own, four heroes yours, begging, sent, I.
sentences.i: From my own son I have sent to ask for your four heroes.
sentences.n: Köġün-eče-ġen is 'from (my) own son': the reflexive -ġen points back to the speaker, Wang Qan, so the son is his own, most likely Senggum (compare köġün-ü-ġen in the speech below), and not Chinggis, whom he does not yet call son. Why the ablative 'from' stands I cannot tell (perhaps 'on my son's account'). Then čin-u says 'your', turning to Chinggis. külüġüd: külüg + plural, Ming 傑 'outstanding men'; the four are named two units on. γujužu: Ming 索着, 'asking for'.

morph.gloss: hero, outstanding man (Ming 傑) [傑(每行)]
to ask for, seek (Ming 索) [索着]

sentences.t: Irge orγo min-u aburažu ögtügei" keġežü iležüġüi.
sentences.l: People, household mine, saving, let-give," saying, sent-off.
sentences.i: "Rescue my people and household and give them back," he said, and sent him off.
sentences.n: ögtügei is ög- 'give' + -tügei, a third-person optative, Ming 與者; I take it as a request that Chinggis give them back. aburažu is abura- 'save, rescue' (Ming 救着). keġežü iležüġüi is 'saying, sent off' (Ming 去了來). Wang Qan is the speaker.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan tende Boγ̇orču, Muqali, Boroγul, Čilaγ̇un-Baγ̇atur ede dörben külüġüd(i)-jen čerig žasažu ilebe.
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan there Boγ̇orču, Muqali, Boroγul, Čilaγ̇un-Baγ̇atur, these four heroes-ACC-own army arraying, sent.
sentences.i: There Chinggis Qahan got an army in order and sent off these four of his heroes: Bo'orchu, Muqali, Boroqul and Chila'un Ba'atur.
sentences.n: The four names are those of the külüġüd, 'the four heroes'; Shiratori's commas separate them and each is glossed 人名 (the last adds 勇士). külüġüd(i)-jen is külüg + plural + (i) accusative + 'own'. Ming 敎去了 'caused to go'.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Chila'un Ba'atur (name with the title baγ̇atur, 'hero') [人名 勇士]
hero, outstanding man (Ming 傑) [傑(每) 自的行]
to put in order, array (Ming 整治) [整治着]

sentences.t: ede dörben külüġüd-i kürküi-jin urida Hulaγ̇an-Qud-ta Seṅgüm bailduqu bolun morin-u-γ̇an γuja qaγdažu abdaqu bolžu büküi-dür
sentences.l: These four heroes arriving-of before, Hulaγ̇an-Qud-at Seṅgüm, battle-facing-about becoming, horse-of-own leg being-shot, being-seized-about becoming, being-when,
sentences.i: Before these four heroes arrived, when Senggum, who was about to give battle at Hula'an-Qud, had his horse shot in the leg and was on the point of being taken,
sentences.n: kürküi-jin urida is 'before the arriving', participle + genitive + 'before'. The accusative -i on külüġüd-i (Ming 行) is odd beside an intransitive participle; I read it as marking 'these four' as the ones arriving, but that is a guess. Hulaγ̇an-Qud-ta is a place (Ming 地名). bailduqu is 'about to face battle' (as baildun above). morin-u-γ̇an γuja is 'own horse's leg' (Ming 馬自的 腿). qaγdažu: Ming 被射着 'being shot' (passive of a stem I infer). abdaqu is ab- 'take' + passive + -qu, 'about to be taken'. This is the time clause for the next unit.

morph.gloss: hero, outstanding man (Ming 傑) [傑(每行)]
to face in battle order, join battle [對陣]
to shoot (stem inferred from Ming 射) [被射着]

sentences.t: ede dörben külüġüd kürčü aburaγ̇ad irge orγa eme köġü bügüde-ji aburažu ögbe.
sentences.l: These four heroes arriving, saved, people, household, wife, son, all-ACC saving, gave.
sentences.i: these four heroes arrived and made the rescue, and, saving them all, people, household, wife and son, gave them back.
sentences.n: The first aburaγ̇ad has no object; whom the heroes saved is not stated. I leave it open ('made the rescue') rather than supply Senggum. bügüde-ji is 'all' with an accusative (Ming 都 行). ögbe 'gave' has no stated recipient; 'gave them back' is the sense of the sequence.

morph.gloss: household, tent-folk (Ming 人烟 'smoke of people') [人烟]

sentences.t: Tende Waṅ-Qān ügülerün:
sentences.l: There Waṅ-Qān speaking:
sentences.i: Then Wang Qan said:
sentences.n: Tende is 'there' (Ming 那裏); I read it as 'thereupon'. The speech runs to the keġebe that closes the section.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, a ruler's name (Ming 人名 'a person's name') [人名]

sentences.t: "Erte sain ečige-de in-ü ene metü odun baraγsan ulus(i)-jan aburažu ögteleġe.
sentences.l: "Formerly good father-by, his, this like, gone ruined people-ACC-own saving, was-given.
sentences.i: "Long ago, by his good father, in this way, my own people who had gone to ruin were rescued and given back.
sentences.n: A first reading. ečige-de is 'to / by the father'; in-ü 'his' (Chinggis's), so 'his good father', which I take as Jesügei, whom Wang Qan names in the next §. ene metü is 'like this'. odun baraγsan: 'gone (and) ruined', od- 'go' + bara-; ulus(i)-jan is 'people-ACC-own', with the accusative bracketed. ögteleġe is a passive (Ming 被與了 'was given'), and the dative on the father then marks the agent.

morph.gloss: his (third-person genitive, front-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]

sentences.t: Edöġe basa köġün-ü-ġen odun baraγsan ulus-i min-u dörben külüġüd(i)-jen irežü aburažu ögtebe.
sentences.l: Now again son-of-own gone ruined people-ACC, mine four heroes-own coming, saving, was-given.
sentences.i: Now again my own son's people, who had gone to ruin, have been rescued by my four heroes, who came, and given back.
sentences.n: Doubtful. köġün-ü-ġen is 'of (his) own son', which I take as Senggum, whose family and people were the ones taken. min-u dörben külüġüd(i)-jen is Ming 我的 四傑 'my four heroes'; printed min-u 'my', as Wang Qan speaks of Chinggis's champions. irežü is ire- 'come' + -žü. The passive ögtebe (Ming 被與了) again has the object in the accusative.

morph.gloss: hero, outstanding man (Ming 傑) [傑(每) 自的行]

sentences.t: Hači qariγ̇ulqu-ji teṅgeri γažar-un igeġel medetügei" keġebe.
sentences.l: "Enmity returning-ACC, heaven earth's protecting-help let-know," said.
sentences.i: "As for returning the enmity, may the protecting help of Heaven and Earth know it," he said.
sentences.n: Hači is glossed 讎 'enmity', and qariγ̇ulqu-ji is 'the returning' (qari- 'return' + causative). So 'to return a hači' could mean to take vengeance or, in this context of a rescue, to repay a debt; the glosses decide neither way, and I keep the word they give. igeġel is Ming 護助 'protection and help'; medetügei is mede- 'know' + -tügei, 'let ... know'.

morph.gloss: requital, a debt of enmity or favour to be paid (Ming 讎 'enmity'; sense uncertain) [讎]
protecting help, aid (Ming 護助; stem uncertain) [護助]

sentences.t: Basa Waṅ-Qān ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Waṅ-Qān speaking:
sentences.i: Again Wang Qan said:
sentences.n: Basa 'again' (Ming 再). The speech that follows runs to alduba's unit at the end of §164; I cut it into its sentences.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, a ruler's name (Ming 人名 'a person's name') [人名]

sentences.t: "Jesügei-Baγ̇atur anda min-u odun baraγsan ulus min-u nigente aburažu ögbe.
sentences.l: "Jesügei-Baγ̇atur, sworn-brother mine, gone ruined people mine, once saving, gave.
sentences.i: "My sworn brother Yesügei Ba'atur once rescued my people, who had gone to ruin, and gave them back.
sentences.n: Jesügei-Baγ̇atur: Jesügei (Yesügei in the English), with the title baγ̇atur (Ming 勇士); he is the father of Chinggis, as the glosses later make plain (父). nigente: nigen 'one' + dative, Ming 一次行 'once'. This repeats, as a statement, what the previous § said in the passive.

morph.gloss: Yesügei Ba'atur (name with the title baγ̇atur, 'hero') [人名 勇士]
sworn brother (Ming 契交 'pledged friend') [契交]
dative-locative: at one time, once (Ming 一次行)

sentences.t: Temüžin köġün basa oduγsan ulus min-u aburažuγ̇u ögbe.
sentences.l: Temüžin son again gone people mine saving-(past) gave.
sentences.i: Temüjin, the son, has again rescued my people who had gone away and given them back.
sentences.n: Temüžin köġün is two nouns side by side, 'Temüjin (the) son' (Ming 兒子), no 'my' in the Mongol. oduγsan (Ming 去了的) is 'the one that has gone', a plainer word than odun baraγsan, 'gone and ruined', above. aburažuγ̇u: past -žuγ̇u, with a Ming 也 for emphasis.

morph.gloss: past participle: 'one that has gone' (Ming 去了的)

sentences.t: Ede ečige köġün qojar odun baraγsan ulus na-da qurijažu ögürün ken-ü emüne qurijažu ögün žobomui.
sentences.l: These father son the-two, gone ruined people, me-to gathering, giving-when, whose front gathering, giving, toil is.
sentences.i: These two, father and son, gathered up for me the people who had gone and been ruined, and gave them to me; in front of whom would they gather them up and give them? It is toil.
sentences.n: na-da is 'to me' (na- the oblique stem of bi). qurijažu is Ming 收拾着 'gathering up, putting in order'; ögürün is ög- 'give' + -ürün 'when giving'. Ming 兩箇 'the two' for qojar. Not understood from ken-ü on: ken-ü emüne is Ming 誰的前面 'in front of whom'; žobomui is žobo- (Ming 生受 'suffer hardship') in the present, 'is toil'. I cannot say what 'in front of whom' means, and my English only shapes it into a question, which is a guess; 'else' is not in the Mongol and is not put in.

morph.gloss: the two, a pair (of persons) [兩箇]
to gather up, put in order (Ming 收拾) [收拾着]
in front of, before (Ming 前面) [前面]
to gather up, put in order (Ming 收拾) [收拾着]
to toil, suffer hardship (Ming 生受) [生受有]

sentences.t: Bi ber edöġe ötölbe.
sentences.l: I also now have-grown-old.
sentences.i: I too have grown old now.
sentences.n: ber is Ming 也 'also'. ötölbe, 'has grown old', is ötöl- + -be (Ming 老了).

sentences.t: Nama-ji ötölžü ündüd-te γaruγ̇asu qaγ̇učidba bi.
sentences.l: Me, growing-old, on-heights going-up-when, grew-worn, I.
sentences.i: Now that I am old, if I go up on the heights I wear out;
sentences.n: nama-ji is 'me' with the accusative, which I take as 'as for me' (Ming 我行 'to me'). ündüd-te: Ming 高處 'high places', plural, with the locative. γaruγ̇asu is γar- 'go up/out' + 'if'. qaγ̇učidba is Ming 舊了, 'has grown old, worn'. The picture is of a ruler too old for the hard places; the glosses give no more than the words.

morph.gloss: high (the glossary's ündür); plural -d, 'high places' (Ming 高處; the r does not show) [高處(每)行]
to go up, go out [上呵]
conditional: 'if, when' (a linking u, then -γ̇asu; Ming 呵)
to grow old, worn out (Ming 舊) [舊了]

sentences.t: Qaγ̇učidču qaldud-ta γaruγ̇asu qamuγ ulus ken medekü.
sentences.l: Worn-out, on-crags going-up-when, all people who will-manage?
sentences.i: worn out, if I go up on the crags, who will manage all the people?
sentences.n: qaldud-ta is Ming 崖每行 'on the crags' (plural); qamuγ ulus is 'all the people' (Ming 普 百姓). ken is 'who'; medekü is mede- 'know' with a future participle, Ming 管 'manage, have charge of'.

morph.gloss: to grow old, worn out (Ming 舊) [舊了着]
cliff, crag (Ming 崖; stem inferred) [崖每行]
to go up, go out [上呵]
conditional: 'if, when' (a linking u, then -γ̇asu; Ming 呵)
to know, to manage (Ming 管) [管]

sentences.t: Deġü-ner min-u abur-i ügeigün bi.
sentences.l: Brothers mine virtue-without-ones, are.
sentences.i: My younger brothers have no goodness in them.
sentences.n: Deġü-ner is deġü 'younger brother' + the plural -ner (Ming 弟每). abur-i is printed with a hyphen but is probably the one word aburi (Han 阿不舌里), 'disposition' in the glossary (Ming 性兒); here the Ming is 德行 'conduct, virtue', and the hyphen's -i I do not treat as an ending. ügeigün, Ming 無每 'those without', I cannot analyse beyond ügei 'without'. The bi here is the verb (Ming 有) 'is', not 'I'. The text does not name the brothers.

morph.gloss: disposition, conduct (Ming 德行 'conduct, virtue'; printed abur-i, the -i probably part of the noun, cf. aburitu 'having a temper') [德行]
ending of unclear sense (Ming 無每 with the plural 每)
is, there is (the verb 'to be'; Ming 有) [有]

sentences.t: Γaγča köġün min-u ügei metü Seṅgüm γaγča bijü.
sentences.l: Alone son mine not-being like, Seṅgüm alone is.
sentences.i: I have one son only, and it is as if I had none: Senggum stands alone.
sentences.n: A first reading, from the Ming 獨子我的無般桑昆獨有 'a single son of mine, like none; Senggum alone is'. ügei metü is 'like not-being'; I take it as saying that his one son is of no use to him. γaγča 'alone' is repeated.

sentences.t: Temüžin köġün-i Seṅgüm-ün aqa bolγažu qojar köġütü bolžu amu- suγai"
sentences.l: Temüžin son-ACC, Seṅgüm's elder-brother making, two sons-having becoming, rest-may-I."
sentences.i: "Making Temüjin, the son, elder brother to Senggum, and so having two sons, may I rest."
sentences.n: köġün-i: 'the son' (Ming 子行) with the accusative; the Mongol has no 'my'. bolγažu is bol- + causative -γa- (Ming 做着), 'making'. köġütü: 'son-having'. amu- and suγai are one word split across the line, 'may I rest', the -suγai first-person optative (Ming 我). The speech closes here.

morph.gloss: the two, a pair (of persons) [兩箇]
to rest (the stem; the ending stands on the next word) [歇息]
optative, first person: 'may I' (Ming 我) [我]

sentences.t: keġežü Čiṅgis Qaγan-luγ̇a Waṅ-Qān Tuγ̇ula-jin Qara tün-(n)e qurižu ečige köġü keġeldübe.
sentences.l: Saying, Čiṅgis Qaγan-with Waṅ-Qān, Tuγ̇ula's Black Forest-in assembling, father, son, said-together.
sentences.i: Having said this, Wang Qan met Chinggis Qahan in the Black Forest of the Tula, and the two agreed together as father and son.
sentences.n: -luγ̇a (Ming 一同) 'with', placed after Qaγan, so Wang Qan is the subject. Tuγ̇ula-jin Qara tün-(n)e is 'in the Tula's Black Forest' (Ming 地名的 黑 林行). keġeldübe is keġe- 'say' + reciprocal -ldü- (Ming 共說了 'said together'); ečige köġü 'father (and) son' is what they said to one another, so I read it as a pact of father and son.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Wang Qan, a ruler's name (Ming 人名 'a person's name') [人名]
Tula, a river name [地名 的]
to gather, assemble (Ming 聚會) [聚會着]

sentences.t: Ečige köġün keġeldüküi josun urida erte üdür Jesügei Qān ečige- lüġe Waṅ-Qān anda keġeldügsen josu-γ̇ar ečige metü keġežü
sentences.l: Father, son, said-together-of principle, formerly, earlier days, Jesügei Qān, father-with, Waṅ-Qān, sworn-brother, said-together-which principle-by, father like saying,
sentences.i: The principle of the father-and-son pledge, from the days of old, when Yesügei Qan, the father, and Wang Qan, as sworn brothers, agreed together, and by the terms they agreed said "like a father,"
sentences.n: A first reading. josun is Ming 道理 'rule, reason, principle'. keġeldüküi is the participle of keġeldü- 'say together', 'of the saying-together'. urida erte üdür is 'before, early, day', Ming 先 在前 日子 'the days of old'. There is no verb in the Mongol after üdür, so the English leaves the clause open; the next unit resumes it with teimü. ečige- and lüġe are one word, 'with the father' (Ming 父, 一同), split by the line; the father is Jesügei, whom the Ming calls 皇帝 (Qān) here. keġeldügsen josu-γ̇ar is 'according to the principle that was said together' (Ming 共說了的道理依著). ečige metü keġežü is 'saying "like a father"', the speaker not named.

morph.gloss: rule, principle, reason (Ming 道理) [道理]
Wang Qan, a ruler's name (Ming 人名 'a person's name') [人名]
sworn brother (Ming 契交 'pledged friend') [契交]
rule, principle (variant of josun) [道理 依着]

sentences.t: ečige köġün keġeldüküi josu teimü üge ügüleldürün:
sentences.l: Father, son, said-together-of principle thus; word speaking-together:
sentences.i: that principle of the father-and-son pledge was this; and as they spoke together, the words were these:
sentences.n: teimü is Ming 那般有 'so it is, thus'. ügüleldürün is ügüle- 'speak' + reciprocal + 'when', Ming 共說. The colon opens the pact itself, which runs to keġeldübe in the next two units.

morph.gloss: rule, principle (variant of josun) (Ming 道理) [道理]
so it is, thus (Ming 那般有) [那般有]

sentences.t: "Olon daisun-dur qaγ̇ulurun qamtu nigen-e qaγ̇uluja;
sentences.l: "Many enemy-against campaigning-when, together one-in campaign-let-us;
sentences.i: "When we go to war against many enemies, let us go to war together, as one;
sentences.n: qaγ̇ul- is a stem I infer from Ming 征 'campaign'; the Ming for daisun-dur is 敵行 'to the enemy' (the Han is 歹亦孫突兒). nigen-e is 'in one' (Ming 一處 'one place'). Shiratori's semicolon ends the first clause.

morph.gloss: to go to war, campaign (stem inferred from Ming 征; the glossary has qaγ̇ul- 'raid, plunder, rush' for what may be the same verb) [征時]
to go to war, campaign [征咱]
optative, first person plural: let us (Ming 咱)

sentences.t: oroγ̇a göreġešün-dür dabalarun nigen-e kü qamtu abalaja" keġeldübe.
sentences.l: wild beasts-for ring-hunting-when, one-in also together ring-hunt-let-us," said-together.
sentences.i: when we hunt the wild game in the ring, let us hunt in one company too," they agreed.
sentences.n: Shiratori prints dabalarun, but the Han 阿把剌舌侖 give abalarun, and the verb is abalaja two words on (Ming 圍獵咱 'let us hunt in a ring'). I follow the Han and Ming, so the stem is abala-. oroγ̇a göreġešün-dür is 'for wild beasts' (Ming 野 獸行). kü is Ming 也, a particle I render 'too'. keġeldübe closes the pact.

morph.gloss: to hunt in a ring-battue (Ming 圍獵; Shiratori prints dabalarun, the Han give abalarun) [圍獵時]
just, indeed (emphatic particle; Ming 也) [也]
to hunt in a ring-battue (Ming 圍獵) [圍獵咱]

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Waṅ-Qān qojar ügüleldürün:
sentences.l: Again Čiṅgis Qaγan, Waṅ-Qān, the-two, speaking-together:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan and Wang Qan, the two of them, spoke together:
sentences.n: Basa 'again'; ügüleldürün as before. A second pledge follows, on slander.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Wang Qan, a ruler's name (Ming 人名 'a person's name') [人名]
the two, a pair (of persons) [兩箇]

sentences.t: "Bida qojar-i naidažu šüdütü moγaj-a südürteġesü südürgen-dür bu oroja;
sentences.l: "We-two-ACC envying, tooth-having snake-by, being-incited-if, incitement-into not enter-let-us;
sentences.i: "If the snake with teeth, envying us two, should set us against each other, let us not fall into its inciting;
sentences.n: naidažu is naida- 'envy' (Ming 嫉妬着); I give the snake as the subject, but it could also qualify us. šüdütü is šüdü 'tooth' + -tü, Ming 牙有的. moγaj-a: 'snake' with a dative that is the agent after a passive, südürteġesü (südür- 'incite', Ming 挑唆, + passive + 'if'). bu oroja is 'let us not enter'. The snake is a figure of the slanderer; so the context (inciting, parting) suggests, though the glosses give only 'snake'.

morph.gloss: to envy, be jealous of (Ming 嫉妬) [嫉妬着]
to incite, set against one another (Ming 挑唆) [被挑唆呵]
do not (prohibitive particle; Ming 休) [休]
optative, first person plural: let us (Ming 咱)

sentences.t: südü-ġer ama-γ̇ar ügüleldüžü büšireje;
sentences.l: tooth-with, mouth-with speaking-together, let-us-trust;
sentences.i: let us speak together with tooth and mouth, and trust;
sentences.n: südü-ġer and ama-γ̇ar are 'with tooth' and 'with mouth' (Ming 牙依着, 口依着). I take the pair as 'face to face', the opposite of the snake's whispering, but that is my reading; the glosses give only the two tools. büšire- is Ming 信 'to trust', with -je 'let us'.

morph.gloss: tooth (Ming 牙; printed südü here, šüdü in šüdütü, the same Han 速都) [牙(依着)]
optative, first person plural: let us (Ming 咱)

sentences.t: araγ̇atu moγaj-a adardaγ̇asu adarγan-i in-ü bu abulčaja.
sentences.l: big-toothed snake being-parted-if, parting-ACC his not take-together-let-us.
sentences.i: and if the great-fanged snake should part us, let us not take up its dividing together.
sentences.n: araγ̇atu: Ming 大牙有的 'having great teeth'; I infer the stem araγ̇a 'fang' from the gloss alone. adardaγ̇asu is adar- 'part, set apart' (Ming 離間) + passive + 'if'. in-ü is 'his', the snake's. abulčaja is ab- 'take' + the joint-action suffix -ulča- (Ming 共要咱), 'let us take (it) together'.

morph.gloss: great tooth, fang (Ming 大牙; stem inferred) [大牙有的]
to part, set apart (Ming 離間 'sow discord between') [(被離間呵)]
parting, sowing of division (Ming 離間) [(離間行)]
his (third-person genitive, front-vowel form, set after its noun) [他的]
do not (prohibitive particle; Ming 休) [休]
optative, first person plural: let us

sentences.t: Ama-γ̇ar kele-ġer olulčažu büšireje" keġen tein üge baraldužu amaγ̇aralin alduba.
sentences.l: Mouth-with, tongue-with confronting-together, let-us-trust," saying, such word settling, closely, together passed.
sentences.i: "Let us face each other with mouth and tongue, and trust," they said; and having settled such terms, in close friendship they passed their time together.
sentences.n: olulčažu: Ming 對證着 'confronting each other, checking against'; the stem is uncertain. keġen closes the speech. amaγ̇aralin is glossed 親厚着 'being close'; I take it as 'closely' and cannot analyse it. alduba is al- (stem inferred from Ming 過 'pass') + reciprocal -du- (Ming 共) + -ba; 'passed together' is the Ming's, and what is passed (the time? the days?) is not stated. Last unit of the part.

optative, first person plural: let us (Ming 咱)
to settle together, agree (stem inferred; Ming 議定 'settle') [議定着]
